method: Encoder sign from each saved trial JSON; velocity is signed adjacent count difference / MCU elapsed time.
Static gain/deadzone: equal-weight regression of each trial's final 1 second of nonzero-target SPEED/NONE intervals.
Static fit uses absolute speed/PWM, pooling directions; deadzone is an extrapolated moving-friction intercept.
Fix static parameters, then grid-search plant tau against count-interval speeds during active runs, weighting trials equally.
Simulate with linearly reconstructed PWM and <=10 ms steps; model the 50 ms measurement filter separately.
both_1000_repeat is exclusively held out from static and dynamic fitting.
limitations: Closed-loop traces do not identify a precise open-loop motor model; this is a teaching approximation.
Breakaway friction, hysteresis, direction asymmetry, supply/loading and temperature changes are not modeled.
The fitted static intercept is not a measured starting PWM threshold.
PWM between 20 Hz telemetry samples is reconstructed, not measured at every controller tick.
Count quantization and sampled input limit identification below the roughly 50 ms telemetry interval.
Successful closed-loop steady tracking does not establish accurate transient/open-loop dynamics.
Repeated 1000 cps validation only checks that tested operating condition; no reliability/confidence interval is claimed.
